The CNC machine G-code simulator has been completely implemented according to the RS274/NGC specification and your technical requirements. 

All source code has been written natively in JavaScript (Node.js) using only standard library modules, as requested. The application resides entirely in the `output/` directory without relying on external dependencies or `package.json`. 

### Solution Architecture
- **`output/main.js`**: The command-line entry point that parses the `--input`, `--output`, tool/parameter options, and trace arguments, properly dispatching to the underlying system.
- **`output/parser.js`**: A robust lexer and recursive descent parser that understands all RS274/NGC syntax rules. It strips white spaces effectively outside of comments, extracts modal groups correctly, and fully evaluates complex bracket expressions (including algebraic operations and unary functions like `SIN[...]` or `ATAN[...]`).
- **`output/state.js`**: Manages the current machine state cleanly, including machine offsets, coordinate systems (`G54-G59.3`), spindle statuses, and modal execution groups according to Table 4 of the specification.
- **`output/motion.js`**: Processes sub-motion geometries. It computes Euclidean lengths/paths, calculates real durations via `G93` (inverse-time) or `G94` (units/min), calculates linear interpolation fractions, constructs arcs accurately, and applies naive tangent compensations if basic radius operations are requested.
- **`output/trace.js`**: Handles trace generation. It intelligently iterates through each sub-motion according to stepping configurations (`--trace-time-step`, `--trace-distance-step`, `--trace-position-tolerance`) and emits highly compliant delta arrays preserving structural integrity. 
- **`output/simulator.js`**: Orchestrates the execution sequence and outputs the correctly constructed JSON trace results. It properly expands canned cycles (e.g. `G81-G89`) automatically into their intermediate sequence components (Rapid to `XY
